2026 Appalachian Power RFPs

Appalachian Power (APCo), an American Electric Power company, is pursuing additional thermal Combined Cycle Natural Gas Assets via the following request for proposal (RFP).

RFP Summary

APCo is pursuing up to 1500 MW of accredited nameplate capacity from Combined Cycle Thermal Resources from this RFP. The Resources requested via this RFP will be acquired via PSAs for purchase of 100% of the equity interest of the Project’s limited liability company (Project’s LLC). New PSA Resources will be acquired on or about Substantial Completion. Existing Combined Cycles are also eligible for submission. Projects must be physically located and deliverable to the AEP Locational Deliverability Area (LDA) and interconnected (via Interconnection Agreement or pseudo-tie) to the PJM Transmission system. The Company is pursuing Projects that can achieve COD no later than 3/31/2031.

Proposals will be evaluated based on criteria outlined in the RFP.

Appalachian Power encourages the use of local goods or services sourced, in whole or in part, from one or more Virginia or West Virginia based businesses in the construction and/or operation of the projects or United States-based manufacturers using materials or product components made in Virginia or the United States. Projects must conform to the requirements in the Virginia Environmental Justice Act (Virginia Code §§ 2.2-234, et. seq.).

RFP Schedule

Issue RFPs: August 17, 2026

Proposal Due Date: September 17, 2026

2026 Appalachian Power RFPs

Appalachian Power Company (APCo), an American Electric Power company, is pursuing additional Energy Storage Assets via the following request for proposals (RFPs).

Communicating with us

Learn when to contact us and how to stay updated during an outage.

RFP Summary (Energy Storage PSA RFP)

APCo is pursuing up to 500 MW of accredited nameplate capacity from Energy Storage Resources from this RFP. The resources requested via this RFP will be acquired via PSAs for purchase of 100% of the equity interest of the Project’s limited liability company (Project’s LLC). New PSA Resources will be acquired on or about Mechanical Completion. Existing Energy Storage Facilities are also eligible for submission. Projects must be physically located and deliverable to the Commonwealth of Virginia and interconnected (via Interconnection Agreement or pseudo-tie) to the PJM Transmission system. The Company is pursuing Projects that can achieve COD targeted for CODs no later than 3/31/2030, however, proposals with later CODs will also be considered.

RFP Summary (Energy Storage CPA RFP)

APCo is pursuing up to 300MW purchases of electric capacity from Energy Storage resources within the PJM region that will enable APCo to satisfy its load and planning reserve obligations. The Energy Storage resource must have accredited Installed Available Capacity that satisfies the qualifications of the PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff and the PJM Rules to provide Accredited UCAP to APCo. Additionally, Bidders must have 100% ownership of the asset or have documented authority to offer the asset into the RFP.

Proposals will be evaluated based on criteria outlined in the RFPs.

Appalachian Power Company encourages the use of local goods or services sourced, in whole or in part, from one or more Virginia or West Virginia based businesses in the construction and/or operation of the projects or United States-based manufacturers using materials or product components made in Virginia or the United States. Projects must conform to the requirements in the Virginia Environmental Justice Act (Virginia Code §§ 2.2-234, et. seq.).

Proposal Due Date: September 30, 2026

2026 Appalachian Power RFPs

Appalachian Power (APCo), an American Electric Power company, is pursuing additional wind and solar generation resources, along with hydro and geothermal resources, via the following requests for proposals (RFPs)*.

The RFPs are as follows:

  • Wind and Solar (PSA): Up to 800 MW wind and/or solar resource RFP via one or more purchase and sale agreements (PSAs) for purchase of 100% equity interest in a project company. Bidders may propose build-transfer or development stage projects that achieve a commercial operation date of no later than Dec. 31, 2029. To qualify for consideration, projects must interconnect to the PJM Interconnection L.L.C. RTO or the APCo distribution system and be located within the PJM footprint. APCo has a preference for projects located in Virginia or West Virginia.. Projects that interconnect to PJM must be at least 50 MW in size for wind and solar. In addition, projects that interconnect to the APCo distribution system must be at least 10 MW in size.
  • Wind, Solar, Hydro and Geothermal (PPA): Up to 300 MW wind, solar, and/or hydro RFP via one or more long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs) for the purchase of the energy, capacity, and environmental attributes (including renewable energy certificates) from the project. To qualify, projects must be operational by Dec. 31, 2029, and must meet the minimum nameplate rated (MWac) size as follows: solar (5 MW), wind (50 MW), and hydro (20 MW). Additionally, projects must interconnect to the PJM Interconnection L.L.C. RTO or the APCo Distribution system.
  • Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs): RFP for renewable energy certificates produced from eligible renewable resources. Bidders may submit proposals for contract terms between 5 years and 30 years beginning Jan. 1, 2027, 2028, or 2029; alternative terms will also be considered.

Proposals will be evaluated based on criteria outlined in the RFPs.

Appalachian Power encourages the use of local goods or services sourced, in whole or in part, from one or more Virginia based businesses in the construction and/or operation of the projects or United States-based manufacturers using materials or product components made in Virginia or the United States. Projects must conform to the requirements in the Virginia Environmental Justice Act (Virginia Code §§ 2.2-234, et. seq.).

APCo plans to issue a separate RFP for Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) resources in Q3/Q4 of 2026 in accordance with the recently passed Virginia House Bill 895, which amended and reenacted § 56-580 and § 56-585.5 of the Code of Virginia by adding in Subtitle V of Title 45.2 a chapter numbered 22, consisting of a section numbered § 45.2-2120, relating to electric utilities; energy storage resources; Department of Energy to develop model ordinances; work groups; reports.
